subject.title: Rebrand text-substitution filter on tool-call arguments silently misroutes file ops

question: What should the permanent safety boundary be for plugin text transforms when a replacement matches executable tool arguments or filesystem-like strings?
rationale: The code path is real, but changing it can break existing plugin/provider compatibility because current docs describe output transforms as applying before tool execution.

options.title: Protect executable/path strings by default
options.body: Keep display and prompt compatibility transforms, but skip or require explicit opt-in for path-like and tool-bearing argument values, then document and test the boundary.

options.title: Adopt the linked path-aware PR shape
options.body: Use the open fork PR as the implementation base after maintainers decide that its delimiter heuristic and opt-out behavior are the desired contract.

options.title: Preserve current transform semantics
options.body: Keep current broad replacements and instead add diagnostics or migration guidance, accepting that plugins can rewrite executable argument strings.

recommendation.title: Protect executable/path strings by default
recommendation.body: Keep display and prompt compatibility transforms, but skip or require explicit opt-in for path-like and tool-bearing argument values, then document and test the boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The text-transform feature and current helper surface trace back most clearly to steipete's commits, and the decision is about that public plugin/provider boundary.
